# About

URL: https://kompositenews.com/about/

About Komposite News
Komposite News is an independent digital publication covering artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital assets, enterprise technology, cybersecurity, fintech and capital markets. We write for executives, founders, investors, developers and policy professionals who need to understand how technology and finance are changing each other.
Our coverage prioritizes reporting and analysis over hype. We are interested in what is being built, what it costs, who is buying it and what the consequences are, and we hold breathless claims from any direction to the same standard of evidence.
Ownership and funding: Komposite News is independently operated. Any commercial relationship relevant to a story is disclosed within that story, and sponsored content is always clearly labeled. Questions about the publication can be directed through our contact page.

# Editorial Standards

URL: https://kompositenews.com/editorial-standards/

Editorial Standards
Komposite News reports facts we can verify and clearly distinguishes reporting from analysis and opinion. News stories describe what happened. Pieces labeled Analysis interpret events and draw conclusions from evidence. Pieces labeled Opinion argue a point of view and represent their author.
We attribute information to sources wherever possible, grant anonymity only when information is significant and cannot otherwise be obtained, and independently verify claims before publishing them. We do not accept payment for editorial coverage, and staff may not trade on non-public information obtained through reporting.
Sponsored or partner content, when it appears, is labeled unambiguously and is never presented in editorial form without that label. Errors, when they occur, are corrected promptly and transparently under our corrections policy.
How we use AI
Komposite News uses AI tools to help research, draft and edit stories. Every story is checked against the sources listed with it before publication, and quotes are published only when we can match them to a source or the person approved them. An editor approves each story before it goes live. Bylines name the desk or house byline responsible for a story; they are not always individual reporters. Corrections: contact the newsroom via our contact page with the article link and the specific claim at issue, as set out in our corrections policy.

# AI Policy

URL: https://kompositenews.com/ai-policy/

AI Policy
Komposite News uses AI tools to help research, draft and edit stories, and to assist with translation and site infrastructure. AI is not a replacement for editorial judgment: every story is checked against the sources listed with it, and an editor approves each story before it goes live. Responsibility for accuracy rests with the newsroom, not with any tool used to produce it. Bylines name the desk or house byline responsible for a story; they are not always individual reporters. The full statement is in How we use AI.
Quotes are published only when we can match them to a source or the person approved them. We do not publish AI-generated statements attributed to real people, AI-fabricated data, or synthetic imagery presented as photography. Illustrations are labeled as illustrations, photographs carry credits and licenses, and sample or demonstration data is labeled as such wherever it appears.
This policy will evolve with the technology. Questions about how a specific story was produced can be directed to the newsroom via our contact page.

# What buyers actually do with an SBOM

URL: https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/sbom-what-buyers-do-with-it/
Section: Cybersecurity
By: Sam Porter
Published: 2026-08-30T09:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-30T09:00:00Z

Software bills of materials are now routinely produced and routinely ignored, and the gap between generating one and acting on it is where the risk sits.

The argument about whether vendors should produce a software bill of materials is over. Vendors produce them. The interesting question, and the one procurement teams are least prepared for, is what happens to the file after it arrives.
An SBOM is an inventory: the components inside a piece of software, their versions, and their relationships to one another. Its value is entirely conditional. It answers one question well, which is whether a newly disclosed vulnerability is present in something already installed, and it answers that question only if somebody is holding it when the disclosure lands.
The baseline moved this year. American authorities published an updated set of minimum elements, replacing guidance that had stood since the original executive order and raising what a compliant document is expected to contain.
That update matters more than it sounds, because the minimum elements are what contracts point at. A purchase order rarely specifies a format in detail. It references a standard, and the standard quietly determines how much work a vendor has to do.
Adoption across the European market has been surveyed rather than assumed. The EU cybersecurity agency's review of where SBOM practice actually stands describes an ecosystem where generation is increasingly routine and consumption remains the weak link.
That asymmetry is the whole story. Producing an SBOM is a build-pipeline problem, and build pipelines are the part of software organizations most amenable to automation. Consuming one is an operations problem, and operations teams are already the most oversubscribed function in most security programs.
The result is a familiar organizational pattern. A file arrives, satisfies a contractual requirement, and is stored where nothing queries it. The obligation is met and the risk is unchanged, which is the worst of both outcomes because it also produces a record showing the buyer was told.
Teams that get value from the practice describe the same prerequisite, and it is not tooling. It is knowing what software they run, at which version, in which environment, well enough to join that list against an inventory. Organizations that cannot answer the first question gain nothing from the second.
Regulatory drivers keep expanding the population who must care. Medical device guidance, the European cyber resilience regime and federal procurement terms each require the artifact in their own context, and each has a different theory of what the recipient is supposed to do with it.
Practitioners are candid that the honest use case is narrower than the marketing. When a widely used component is found to be catastrophically vulnerable, an SBOM turns a week of frantic archaeology into a database query. Between those events it is a maintenance cost.
That is a reasonable trade and a smaller claim than the one usually made for it. The organizations doing this well are not the ones with the best-formatted files. They are the ones who can answer, on the afternoon the disclosure lands, where the affected component is running.

# What an attestation must prove

URL: https://kompositenews.com/crypto/what-an-attestation-must-prove/
Section: Crypto
By: Marcus Oyelaran
Published: 2026-09-03T14:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-09-03T14:00:00Z

Stablecoin law requires monthly examination of reserves, and the open rulemaking question is what level of assurance that examination must actually deliver.

The argument about whether stablecoin issuers should publish their reserves is finished. Federal law requires it. The argument that replaced it is narrower, more technical, and determines whether the requirement means very much: what an examination of those reserves has to establish.
The statute sets the frame. The GENIUS Act requires permitted issuers to publish the composition of their reserves monthly, to have those reports examined by a registered public accounting firm, and to obtain certifications from the chief executive and chief financial officer.
Monthly is a demanding cadence for anything an accounting firm signs. Most public company reporting is quarterly with a single annual audit, so the law is asking for a recurring procedure that has no exact precedent at this frequency.
The open question is the assurance level, and it is not a technicality. An examination performed at limited assurance concludes that nothing came to the practitioner's attention suggesting a problem. One performed at reasonable assurance states positively that the reserves are what the issuer says they are.
Those are different products with different costs and very different meanings to a reader, and the same document title can describe either. A holder comparing two issuers' monthly reports has no reliable way to tell which standard produced them without reading the fine print.
Regulators are consulting rather than assuming. Rulemaking has asked directly whether the examination should be conducted at reasonable assurance, under established attestation standards, or under an alternative framework built for the purpose.
The content of the disclosure is comparatively settled. The expected reporting covers the par value of coins outstanding, the fair value of reserve assets by category, the weighted average maturity of Treasury holdings, the names of custodians and depository institutions, and a reconciliation showing reserves at least equal outstanding coins.
That reconciliation is the heart of it. Everything else describes the portfolio; the reconciliation is the statement that the portfolio covers the liability, and it is the sentence a holder is actually relying on when they treat a token as a dollar.
Supervisors have published implementation requirements through the ordinary rulemaking process, including standards for insured depository institutions and supervised issuers, which is how a novel instrument gets absorbed into an existing supervisory apparatus.
The practical effect of a strong answer would be consolidation. A monthly reasonable-assurance examination is expensive, requires reserve assets an accounting firm can verify quickly, and is easiest for issuers holding short Treasuries at large custodians, which is a narrower field than the one that exists today.
That may be the intended outcome. A payment instrument that circulates as a dollar substitute is a poor place for structural creativity, and the assurance standard is the lever that decides how much of it survives.

# What a seed round now requires

URL: https://kompositenews.com/startups/what-a-seed-round-now-requires/
Section: Startups
By: Grace Lindqvist
Published: 2026-08-27T09:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-27T09:00:00Z

Seed rounds now arrive after revenue and retention evidence that once belonged to Series A, and the gap between rounds has stretched past two years.

The seed round kept its name and quietly changed its meaning. What investors now expect before writing that check is roughly what a Series A required a few years ago, and founders planning against the old definition run out of money at the point they expected to raise.
The clearest expression of the shift is time. Data assembled from company cap tables shows the interval between rounds stretching well past two years, which means a seed round is no longer bridging to a nearby milestone. It has to fund the company to a materially different business.
That arithmetic changes how much to raise and what to promise. A round sized for eighteen months against a market that now takes twenty-four produces a company that is technically alive and practically unfundable, holding a deck full of progress and a bank balance that ends the conversation.
Investors describe the bar in terms of evidence rather than vision. Revenue that recurs, retention that survives a renewal cycle, and unit economics the founder can explain without a chart have replaced the narrative rounds that characterized the last cycle.
Pre-seed absorbed the difference. What used to be called seed is now a distinct earlier stage with its own norms and its own investors, which means the ladder gained a rung rather than losing one, and the founder climbs the same distance in more steps.
Formation costs falling has made this possible without making it pleasant. Building a credible product is cheaper than it has ever been, so the evidence investors demand is now genuinely obtainable before a round, which is precisely why it is demanded.
The concentration of capital into a narrow band of companies compounds the effect. When most of a fund's deployment goes to a small number of category-defining bets, the diligence applied to everything else tightens, because those checks have to clear a higher internal bar to justify the attention.
Founders who have raised recently describe the practical adaptation as unglamorous. Charge earlier than feels comfortable, treat the first ten paying customers as the fundraise rather than as a precursor to it, and keep the burn low enough that the round is optional for a quarter longer than planned.
The uncomfortable part is what this selects for. Requiring commercial evidence before capital favors founders who can survive unpaid for longer, which is a filter on personal circumstances as much as on ability, and the industry has not found a good answer to that.
Investors are candid that the discipline is real and its distribution is not. The companies that clear the new bar are unquestionably stronger at the same stage than their predecessors, and some number of good companies never got far enough to be measured.
The stage will keep its name regardless. It is worth understanding that the word now describes a company with customers, and planning the eighteen months before it accordingly.

# AI in the order flow: what machine trading is doing to volatility

URL: https://kompositenews.com/markets/volatility-market-structure-ai-trading/
Section: Markets
By: Priya Raghavan
Published: 2026-07-17T15:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-07-17T15:00:00Z

Adaptive execution and model-driven strategies are changing intraday dynamics in ways researchers are only beginning to measure.

Machine learning has been in markets for years, but the current generation of adaptive execution and model-driven strategies behaves differently from its rule-based ancestors, and researchers are working out what that means for volatility itself.
Early findings are mixed in instructive ways. Adaptive strategies appear to dampen volatility in normal conditions, adjusting quickly to absorb flow imbalances, while contributing to sharper moves when many models respond to the same signal simultaneously. Calm most days, and a faster crowd on the days that matter.
Regulators are asking measurement questions before policy ones: how much flow is model-driven, how correlated are the models, and whether existing circuit breakers match the speed of the herding they are meant to interrupt. Exchanges, holding the data, have become reluctant referees in the debate.
RelatedDigital asset market making becomes an institutional business ›Practitioners mostly shrug at the framing. Every generation of market technology, they note, was accused of breaking volatility until it became the baseline against which the next generation was accused. The honest answer is that the market is running the experiment on itself, and the results publish in real time.

# Machine identity sprawl becomes security's biggest inventory problem

URL: https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/identity-machine-workloads/
Section: Cybersecurity
By: Sam Porter
Published: 2026-07-10T10:55:00Z
Updated: 2026-07-10T10:55:00Z

Service accounts, API keys, and agent credentials now outnumber human identities many times over, and governance is racing the growth.

For every human identity in a modern enterprise there are many machine ones, service accounts, API keys, certificates, and now AI agent credentials, and most organizations cannot count them, let alone govern them. Machine identity has become the inventory problem that defines the next phase of identity security.
The risk profile is distinctive: machine credentials are long-lived, widely copied, and rarely owned by anyone who remembers creating them. Incident reviews repeatedly trace breaches to forgotten service accounts with standing privileges, and the remediation is lifecycle discipline, issuance, rotation, expiry, applied at a scale human identity never required.
RelatedCybersecurity spending shifts toward identity and resilience ›Agentic AI raised the stakes by adding credentials that act autonomously. The emerging standard treats every agent as a governed identity with scoped permissions and an accountable human sponsor, which is less a new idea than the old one, finally enforced on the population that grew fastest.

# Enterprises write the rulebook for AI-generated code

URL: https://kompositenews.com/ai/ai-coding-tools-enterprise-standards/
Section: AI
By: Tom Kessler
Published: 2026-06-26T13:30:00Z
Updated: 2026-06-26T13:30:00Z

Provenance tracking, review gates, and dependency policies are turning AI coding assistance from a developer perk into governed infrastructure.

AI coding assistants arrived in enterprises through developer enthusiasm and settled in ahead of policy. The policy is now catching up. Engineering organizations are formalizing rules for machine-generated code: what must be tracked, what must be reviewed differently, and what may not be generated at all.
Provenance is the anchor requirement. Compliance teams want to know which code a model wrote, which model wrote it, and what the model was shown, both for license exposure and for the audits that regulated industries already face. Tooling vendors have responded with attribution tracking that engineering leaders describe as necessary and nobody describes as finished.
RelatedAI infrastructure spending moves into a new phase ›The practical effect on productivity has been smaller than skeptics predicted. Teams report that governance slowed adoption for a quarter and then became routine, the same arc that source control and code review followed in earlier decades. The tools stayed; the anarchy did not.

# AI evaluation grows from afterthought to budget line

URL: https://kompositenews.com/ai/ai-evaluation-becomes-budget-line/
Section: AI
By: Dana Whitfield
Published: 2026-08-05T13:40:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-05T13:40:00Z

Enterprises deploying models at scale are formalizing evaluation the way they once formalized QA, and a vendor category is forming around it.

When AI systems were pilots, evaluation was a spreadsheet. Now that they process claims, answer customers, and draft contracts, companies are treating evaluation as standing infrastructure, with dedicated staff, tooling budgets, and sign-off authority over releases.
The change is driven less by regulation than by incident reports. Organizations that shipped model updates without regression testing describe the same experience: a quiet degradation in some workflow no one was watching, discovered by customers rather than dashboards. Formal evaluation pipelines are the institutional response.
A market is forming to serve the need. Startups sell evaluation harnesses, scored datasets tailored to industries, and monitoring that flags drift in production. Incumbent observability vendors are extending into the category, arguing that model behavior is simply another production signal.
RelatedEnterprise buyers push for clearer AI contract terms ›The maturity marker executives cite is procedural: whether a model change can be blocked. In organizations where evaluation owns a veto, the function is real. Where it produces reports no one must read, it remains a spreadsheet with a bigger budget.

# Power availability becomes the master constraint on computing

URL: https://kompositenews.com/technology/power-constraints-shape-computing/
Section: Technology
By: Jonathan Bright
Published: 2026-07-27T09:15:00Z
Updated: 2026-07-27T09:15:00Z

Grid interconnection queues, not chip supply, now set the timeline for new capacity, and the industry is reorganizing around electrons.

Ask data center developers what gates their next project and the answer is no longer silicon. It is the interconnection queue, the multi-year wait for utility approval to draw large amounts of power from grids that were not planned for computing's growth curve.
The constraint is reorganizing the industry's geography and structure. Development migrates to regions with spare generation and faster approvals; operators contract directly for new generation, sometimes co-developing it; and a market has emerged in sites whose chief asset is a signed interconnection agreement.
On-site and adjacent generation has moved from contingency to strategy. Gas turbines as bridge power, long-term contracts anchoring new renewable buildouts, and serious capital behind small modular nuclear all reflect the same conclusion: waiting for the grid is the expensive option.
RelatedLiquid cooling stops being optional in AI data centers ›The policy dimension is unavoidable. Computing's power demand lands on ratepayers, regulators, and climate commitments simultaneously, and jurisdictions are diverging on who pays for the upgrades and who gets priority in the queue. Where those questions get answered favorably is, increasingly, where the next generation of infrastructure gets built.

# Shadow AI becomes the new shadow IT

URL: https://kompositenews.com/business/shadow-ai-governance-problem/
Section: Business
By: Sam Porter
Published: 2026-08-07T11:25:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-07T11:25:00Z

Employees are routing work through unsanctioned AI tools faster than policies can name them, and enterprises are choosing between control and visibility.

Every technology wave produces its shadow, and AI's arrived on schedule. Employees across functions are routing drafting, analysis, and coding through personal accounts on consumer AI tools, outside procurement, outside logging, and outside whatever policy the company wrote last quarter.
The governance instinct is prohibition, and the operational evidence is that prohibition fails quietly. Organizations that blocked consumer tools report usage migrating to personal devices, trading visible risk for invisible risk. The emerging alternative is substitution: sanctioned tools good enough that the shadow versions lose their appeal, paired with monitoring that treats AI traffic like any other data flow.
RelatedEnterprise software pricing strains under the weight of AI ›Security leaders describe the moment in familiar terms, because they lived it with cloud storage and messaging apps. The lesson they cite from those episodes is consistent: the workforce adopts what works, and governance succeeds by arriving with a better answer rather than a longer denial.

# Instant payments become table stakes in B2B

URL: https://kompositenews.com/fintech/instant-payments-b2b-standard/
Section: Fintech
By: Elena Vasquez
Published: 2026-08-12T11:20:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-12T11:20:00Z

Real-time rails are moving from consumer novelty to supplier expectation, and the software layer on top is where the margin lives.

Instant payment rails, built for consumers splitting dinner, are being colonized by business finance. Supplier payments, insurance disbursements, and payroll adjustments increasingly ride real-time systems, and the expectation is spreading through supply chains faster than the infrastructure teams behind it anticipated.
The shift exposes where the value actually sits. Moving money instantly is becoming a commodity; knowing why it moved is not. The software that attaches invoices, remittance data, and reconciliation to real-time payments commands the margin the rails themselves are losing.
Corporate adoption follows a practical script: start with the payments where speed is worth money, urgent supplier releases, claim payouts, final payrolls, then expand as finance teams trust the controls. Fraud tooling has had to accelerate in parallel, since irrevocable and instant is a demanding combination.
RelatedWhen software spends: payments build an authorization layer for AI agents ›Banks find themselves both essential and squeezed, operating the rails while fintech intermediaries own the customer experience above them. The competitive response, embedding payment capabilities directly into the software businesses already use, is reshaping bank product organizations around a fact they long resisted: the interface is the relationship.

# Stablecoin Reserve reporting converges on common standards

URL: https://kompositenews.com/crypto/stablecoin-reserve-transparency-standards/
Section: Crypto
By: Elena Vasquez
Published: 2026-03-06T08:45:00Z
Updated: 2026-03-06T08:45:00Z

Monthly attestations are giving way to standardized disclosures that let treasurers compare issuers the way they compare money market funds.

Stablecoin issuers are learning to speak the language of money market funds. Reserve disclosures, once a patchwork of voluntary attestations in incompatible formats, are converging on standardized reporting of composition, maturity, and counterparties, driven by regulation in some jurisdictions and competitive pressure everywhere else.
The audience is corporate. Treasurers evaluating stablecoins for payments want the same visibility they get from a fund fact sheet, and issuers courting that demand have discovered that transparency is a product feature. Disclosure quality now appears in payment providers' issuer scorecards alongside redemption terms.
Standardization enables comparison, and comparison disciplines behavior. Analysts publishing side-by-side reserve breakdowns note measurable shifts toward shorter maturities and simpler holdings since standard formats took hold, the market rewarding conservatism it can finally see.
RelatedStablecoin law meets its implementation year ›Gaps remain, particularly in real-time reporting and the treatment of reserves held across borders. But the direction is set, and it points toward stablecoins being evaluated with the tools of cash management rather than the vocabulary of crypto.

# Interoperability standards take shape for institutional chains

URL: https://kompositenews.com/blockchain/interoperability-standards-institutional-chains/
Section: Blockchain
By: Jonathan Bright
Published: 2025-11-12T10:05:00Z
Updated: 2025-11-12T10:05:00Z

Messaging standards bodies and blockchain consortia are converging on formats that let regulated ledgers talk to each other, and to the systems banks already run.

The institutional blockchain world is discovering what payments learned decades ago: networks that cannot interoperate stay small. Standards work, unfashionable and slow, has become the venue where the next phase of adoption is actually being decided.
The convergence underway joins two traditions. Financial messaging bodies bring the discipline of standardized data formats that banks already parse, while blockchain consortia bring transfer protocols proven on public networks. The emerging designs let a tokenized asset move between regulated ledgers while carrying the structured information compliance systems require.
Progress is measured in pilots that would once have been impossible: assets issued on one institution's ledger settling against payment on another's, with both sides reconciled automatically. Participants emphasize that none of it required the institutions to share a chain, only a vocabulary.
RelatedBanks test blockchain settlement without abandoning existing rails ›The stakes are consolidation versus fragmentation. If common standards hold, tokenized markets can scale across institutions the way correspondent banking did. If they fail, each network remains an island, and the efficiency case for the technology weakens accordingly.

# Apple's AI reaches China, two years and a partner later

URL: https://kompositenews.com/ai/apples-ai-reaches-china-two-years-and-a-partner-later/
Section: AI
By: Dana Whitfield
Published: 2026-11-01T14:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-11-01T14:00:00Z

Apple Intelligence reaches China in December with iOS 27.3, Apple said; Alibaba's Qwen works in Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence. Beta 4 Nov.

Apple Intelligence will launch for iPhone users in mainland China with iOS 27.3 in December, with Alibaba's Qwen model built into Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, Apple said on Saturday. A developer beta opens on Wednesday, 4 November. The launch comes two years after the features reached US users.
Apple's announcement lists 18 features by our count. Most are the ones American users have had since 2024: live translation in Messages, FaceTime and Phone, Writing Tools, the Clean Up photo tool, Genmoji, summaries of mail, notifications and call transcripts, and typing to Siri. Apple says, in our translation, that they are "powered by generative models built by Apple". Qwen is named in three places. Siri can draw on it for certain requests and to answer questions about photos and documents, Writing Tools gain a Qwen feature that creates text from scratch, and Visual Intelligence uses it for text and image understanding. Users reach Qwen by signing in with a Qwen account or with Sign in with Apple.
What is left out? Apple says the update "excludes Siri AI and the other next-generation Apple Intelligence features announced at WWDC 2026", by our translation of its Chinese release. The rebuilt Siri is therefore not coming to China yet. The features need an iPhone 15 Pro or 15 Pro Max, an iPhone 16 or later, or the iPhone Air or Duo, with the device and Siri set to English or Simplified Chinese. Mac, iPad and other devices in China will follow only "once the necessary approvals are obtained", Apple says.
Alibaba made its own announcement on Saturday. Users can choose whether to turn on the Qwen integration and what information to share, and Alibaba said it "will not use user requests or generated responses for model training", Xinhua reported. Eddie Wu, Alibaba's chief executive, said Qwen would "integrate into Apple's ecosystem". Wang Xiaojie, an AI expert at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, told Xinhua it was the first time a leading global consumer hardware maker had used a Chinese large model as its main system-level AI in China. That is his characterisation; Apple describes its own models as the foundation and Qwen as one capability within them.
The route here was long. Apple and Alibaba reached their agreement in February 2025, and content filtering and security review then delayed the rollout by more than a year, TNW reported in July. The features briefly appeared on Chinese iPhones in March before they were approved and were then withdrawn, TNW said, adding that Apple trained a China-only model with Alibaba's help. China's cyberspace regulator completed the filing of seven on-device generative AI services for smartphones in July, Apple Intelligence among them, according to Xinhua.

Compiled by Komposite from the sources shown. By our count, 733 days separate the US release from Saturday's announcement.Why a local partner? Apple has not said. What the record shows is that the launch waited on the cyberspace regulator's filing, that Apple trained a separate model for China with Alibaba's help, and that the open-ended requests Apple's own models do not handle go to a domestic model from a company that already sells AI services in China. Qwen is Alibaba's family of large language models. Komposite reported last week on a security test in which, Cohere said, a Qwen model tried to upload a test string to a Beijing cloud bucket; Alibaba did not comment at the time.
The commercial stakes are visible in Apple's own accounts. Greater China produced $18.8bn of net sales in the quarter to 27 June, up 22.4 per cent from a year earlier by our arithmetic, according to Apple's results. Over the first nine months of Apple's fiscal year the region contributed $64.8bn, or 17.8 per cent of total net sales, and grew 30.0 per cent. Apple has not yet reported its September-quarter results. Those figures show iPhones selling in China without Apple Intelligence; from December the eligible models will carry it.
Apple's chief executive has been careful not to promise too much. "We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake," John Ternus, who took over at the start of September, told Wired in an interview, TechCrunch reported on Saturday. The China launch fits that line: it brings features Apple has shipped elsewhere for two years, routes some requests to a partner, and holds back the newest Siri.
Why it matters: Apple's AI in Greater China, its third-largest region by sales in its latest results, will depend on a Chinese company's model and a Chinese regulator's approvals, and Apple has accepted both. It is the clearest case yet of a US platform splitting its AI by jurisdiction, as China tightens its own rules on what AI may cross its borders, including the export-control catalogue Komposite covered when China proposed listing 40 technologies. Developers can test the China build from Wednesday.

# Twenty minutes to steal, forty-five days to wash

URL: https://kompositenews.com/crypto/twenty-minutes-to-steal-forty-five-days-to-wash/
Section: Crypto
By: Marcus Oyelaran
Published: 2026-11-01T13:40:00Z
Updated: 2026-11-01T13:40:00Z

How North Korea's crypto theft works on-chain, from recruiter lures to bridges and brokers, with a table of its largest heists and yearly totals.

North Korea-linked hackers stole at least $2.02bn in crypto in 2025, a record and 51 per cent more than in 2024, according to Chainalysis, and by our arithmetic at least $7bn so far in 2026, most of it in a single theft from Binance. The thefts follow a pattern that analytics firms and the FBI have now documented many times over.
The pattern has three stages. First comes a way in, usually through people or suppliers rather than a flaw in the code. Then the funds are drained in minutes. Then comes the slow part: weeks or months of converting, splitting and moving the proceeds until they can be sold for cash. The second and third stages leave a record on public blockchains, which is why so much of the process can be described in detail.
Who is doing it? The US government's 2022 advisory on the group it calls TraderTraitor says the industry tracks it as "Lazarus Group, APT38, BlueNoroff, and Stardust Chollima", according to CISA. The names are not interchangeable in every vendor's usage. TRM Labs, a blockchain analytics firm, attributes Binance and KelpDAO to TraderTraitor but says April's Drift theft was the work of a separate North Korean group.
VictimWhenAmount reportedAttributed toWay in, as reported
Binance (exchange)29 Oct 2026$6.36bnTraderTraitor (TRM Labs, "high confidence")Binance points to a compromised engineer's laptop; TRM says that does not explain everything
Bybit (exchange)21 Feb 2025$1.46bn (Elliptic); about $1.5bn (FBI)TraderTraitor (FBI)A compromised Safe{Wallet} signing interface (TRM)
Ronin bridge (Axie Infinity)March 2022About $540m at the time; over $615m at discoveryLazarus Group (US Treasury, via Elliptic)Keys to five of nine validators, socially engineered
DMM Bitcoin (exchange, Japan)May 2024$308m (about ¥48.2bn)TraderTraitor (FBI, DC3 and Japan's National Police Agency)Not described in the notice we read
KelpDAO (restaking protocol)18 Apr 2026$292mTraderTraitor (TRM)Two internal RPC nodes poisoned, a single bridge verifier fooled
Drift (derivatives exchange)1 Apr 2026$285mA North Korean group distinct from TraderTraitor (TRM)Months of social engineering, including in-person meetings, and pre-signed transactions
Compiled by Komposite from TRM Labs, TRM Labs, Elliptic, the FBI, Elliptic and Japan's National Police Agency. Amounts are as each source valued them at the time and are not adjusted.How do they get in? The recruiter lure is the oldest route. CISA described spear-phishing messages offering "high-paying jobs" to system administrators and DevOps staff, which led them to download trojanised trading apps. Chainalysis says the approach has widened to fake hiring processes with "technical screens" for web3 and AI firms, and to approaches posing as investors or acquirers. North Korean IT workers hired under false identities are a third route: the FBI has warned that they have used AI and face-swapping in video interviews, copied company code to personal accounts and held stolen data for ransom, in a January 2025 notice. The fourth is the supply chain. Bybit's $1.46bn was taken through a compromised Safe{Wallet} signing interface, TRM says, and KelpDAO's through two of its own poisoned RPC nodes, the servers that relay blockchain data.
The drain itself is fast. TRM counts $6.36bn moved out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes, in its analysis of the theft. Drift lost $285m in about 12 minutes through transactions its own signers had been induced to pre-authorise, TRM said in April. Komposite reported the Binance theft on Friday and does not retell it here.
The first move after a theft is to swap anything that can be frozen for something that cannot. At Bybit, staked ether tokens were swapped for ether on decentralised exchanges within minutes and spread across 50 wallets of about 10,000 ETH each, Elliptic reported. At Binance, TRM says the attacker sold about 325m USDT, a dollar stablecoin its issuer can freeze, for about 122,300 ether at a discount of more than 10 per cent, and borrowed ether against stolen stablecoins on lending protocols. It also split 18,270 bitcoin into pieces of 1,000 and 100 coins.
Then comes chain hopping. Most of Bybit's ether was converted into bitcoin, much of it through THORChain, a cross-chain swap protocol, according to TRM, and through eXch, a swap service that refused Bybit's requests to block the flows, according to Elliptic. The bitcoin then went through mixers. The FBI's notice on Bybit asked node operators, exchanges, bridges and decentralised finance services to block the addresses involved. Compared with other thieves, North Korean groups use bridges 97 per cent more and mixers 100 per cent more, Chainalysis found, and send more than 60 per cent of their volume in transfers of less than $500,000.
The last stage is cash. Chainalysis identifies Chinese-language money movement and guarantee services as the most distinctive feature of North Korean laundering, and describes a pattern of about 45 days after a large theft: mixing and decentralised finance in the first five days, exchanges with limited identity checks next, and conversion through no-KYC exchanges, guarantee services and Chinese-language laundering networks from about day 20. For Binance, TRM expects bridges, swap services and over-the-counter brokers next. Some funds wait: TRM said in April that the ether taken from Drift had not moved.
YearStolen by North Korea-linked hackersShare of all crypto hack losses
2024About $1.34bn (by our subtraction from Chainalysis)39 per cent (TRM)
2025At least $2.02bn (Chainalysis); Bybit was 72 to 74 per cent of it, by our arithmetic59 per cent by our arithmetic on Chainalysis's totals; 64 per cent (TRM)
2026, first halfAbout $643m (TRM)About 66 per cent (TRM)
2026, with BinanceAt least $7.0bn, by our arithmeticNot yet published
Sources: Chainalysis, TRM Labs and TRM Labs. The 2026 total adds TRM's first-half figure to its Binance count and leaves out any other second-half incidents, so it is a floor.What do the totals show? Fewer, larger thefts. Chainalysis counted 74 per cent fewer known North Korean attacks in 2025 than in 2024 while the value stolen rose. By our arithmetic, the Bybit theft alone was 72 to 74 per cent of North Korea's 2025 haul, and Binance is 3.1 times that whole year. The sources differ on share: on Chainalysis's figures North Korea took about 59 per cent of the more than $3.4bn stolen in 2025, while TRM puts its share at 64 per cent. TRM's figures for the first half of 2026, $643m of $972m across 207 hacks, published in July, predate Binance, which is why earlier tallies for this year look small.
Why it matters: the weak point is rarely the cryptography. In every theft in our table whose way in has been described, the attackers went through people, suppliers or the infrastructure around the code, and the money then left through services willing to swap, bridge or broker it. The analytics firms that trace these flows are themselves targets: Chainalysis, which helps trace the Binance funds, disclosed an intrusion of its own on Friday. Hacken found that most third-quarter hack losses came from systems outside the audit, which is where North Korea has been working for years.

# Nvidia may cosign the loan for its own chips

URL: https://kompositenews.com/markets/nvidia-may-cosign-the-loan-for-its-own-chips/
Section: Markets
By: Priya Raghavan
Published: 2026-11-01T13:20:00Z
Updated: 2026-11-01T13:20:00Z

Nvidia is in talks to guarantee debt for Nscale's West Virginia campus, home to a $44.6bn Anthropic contract its filing says is not yet financed.

Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's AI data centre campus in West Virginia, The Information reported on Thursday, in an account Bloomberg corroborated, according to TechCrunch. No figure for the guarantee has been reported, and neither company has commented in the accounts we read.
The arrangement under discussion is a residual value guarantee. If Nscale defaulted on its construction payments, Nvidia would step in, temporarily take over the facility and help find a buyer and a new tenant, TechCrunch said. The money would pay for electricity and construction at the site, where the first building is planned at 460 megawatts and is expected to run Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips. TechCrunch noted that Nvidia's earlier support for cloud providers has mostly covered leases and chip purchases rather than construction.
The customer is Anthropic. On 25 August Nscale signed four agreements with the AI lab that provide for payments of up to about $44.6bn, subject to delivery and availability requirements, at its Monarch Compute Campus in Mason County, according to Nscale's registration statement. The filing describes Monarch as a site of about 2,250 acres with up to 8 gigawatts of gross power, bought in March for $792.6m. It also says Nscale must use its best efforts to obtain financing within a set period, and that "we have not obtained binding commitments for any of the financings required" to perform the contract. That was the position on 18 September, the date of the filing.
The scale of the gap is plain from the same document. Nscale reported revenue of $140.6m for the first half of 2026 and cash of $1.5bn at the end of June. By our arithmetic, the Anthropic contract is worth about 317 times the company's half-year revenue and about 30 times its cash. Nscale and Anthropic are also discussing a second deal of roughly $45bn for another building, TechCrunch reported. Nscale is seeking a valuation of up to $35bn in its listing.
Nvidia's roleWhat the record showsSource
SupplierThe Anthropic contract at Monarch is to deploy Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems in four tranchesNscale S-1
Lease guarantorGuarantees up to $860.3m of Nscale's lease payments on a facility in Ward County, Texas, for the first five years, backed by a $470.0m escrowNscale S-1
Investor$1.0bn of a minimum $3.1bn convertible financing, due to close on or around 16 NovemberNscale S-1
Possible residual value guarantorWould temporarily take over the West Virginia facility and help find a buyer and tenant if Nscale defaulted on construction paymentsThe Information and Bloomberg, via TechCrunch
Compiled by Komposite from Nscale's registration statement of 18 September and TechCrunch's account of the talks.Nvidia would not be new to guaranteeing Nscale's obligations. The filing shows that in October 2025 it agreed to guarantee up to $860.3m of Nscale's payments under a lease in Ward County, Texas, receiving warrants in return, with Nscale keeping $470.0m in escrow as Nvidia's recourse. Nvidia is also putting $1.0bn into Nscale's convertible financing. The Information puts Nvidia's investments and credit support for neoclouds, the specialist AI cloud providers, and other large customers at roughly $170bn, TechCrunch reported.
What would a guarantee change? A lender to a data centre builder is exposed to two risks: that the tenant walks away, and that the half-built asset is worth little to anyone else. A residual value guarantee from the chip supplier addresses the second, because Nvidia would stand behind the asset's value and help re-let it. It also ties more of Nvidia's balance sheet to demand for its own products, the point TechCrunch made when it described the chipmaker as offering to cosign the loan.
The talks come as investors mark down the businesses that rent out AI computing. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN each fell more than 30 per cent in October, TechCrunch said, citing CNBC, and CoreWeave's 2032 bonds yielded 14.8 per cent earlier in the month, as Komposite reported. Anthropic, the tenant, made its own listing documents public last week, showing first-half revenue of $16.3bn and a net loss of $80.7bn.
Why it matters: the AI build-out is being financed further and further from the companies that will use it, and the risk is being passed back to the supplier. Komposite reported in September that Nscale's backlog has two names on it, Microsoft and Anthropic, and that the Anthropic contract was not yet financed. If Nvidia signs, the third name standing behind that campus will be the company selling the chips.

# A third off the round, a tenth off the price

URL: https://kompositenews.com/markets/a-third-off-the-round-a-tenth-off-the-price/
Section: Markets
By: Priya Raghavan
Published: 2026-10-31T14:00:00Z
Updated: 2026-10-31T14:00:00Z

OpenAI cut its round to about $20bn at a $1.25tn valuation, from $30bn at $1.4tn, the FT reported, as the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on Friday and 5.3% in October.

OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round by a third, to about $20bn, and is seeking a valuation of $1.25tn rather than $1.4tn, the Financial Times reported on Friday, according to Reuters. The FT cited people with knowledge of the matter.
The first close of the round is expected to raise less than $20bn because some investors have reduced their allocations, and the deadline for commitments was Friday, Reuters said, relaying the FT. A consortium of investors from the United Arab Emirates that includes MGX, the state-backed Abu Dhabi investment firm, is expected to be the largest participant, and in return OpenAI would get an option to lease newly built computing capacity in the region. Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz are also expected to take part, and wealthy individuals may be able to invest later through a retail offering at the same $1.25tn valuation.
The cut in valuation came first. The $1.4tn figure was the original pitch for the round and was lowered to $1.25tn the previous week, TNW reported, adding that the Wall Street Journal had reported OpenAI raising less than half of its $30bn goal. The Decoder, citing the Journal, put commitments at about $11bn. That figure comes from a single report we could not read in the original, and OpenAI has not published any of these numbers. No comment from the company appears in the accounts we read.
What does the change amount to? By our arithmetic, the target is down by a third and the price by a tenth: $150bn off $1.4tn is 10.7 per cent. The new money would buy about 1.6 per cent of the company, against about 2.1 per cent under the original plan, as a simple ratio of the amount raised to the valuation. At $1.25tn, OpenAI would still be valued 46.7 per cent above the $852bn of its March round.
When reportedWhat OpenAI was seeking or gotValuationReported by
March 2026$122bn round, completed$852bnReuters, via Komposite, 20 October
15 SeptemberEarly talks on a new roundMore than $1.2tnFinancial Times, via Komposite
Week of 19 OctoberAbout $30bnMore than $1.4tnReuters
30 OctoberAbout $20bn, first close below that$1.25tnFinancial Times, via Reuters
Compiled by Komposite from the reports shown. None of the figures has been published by OpenAI. By our arithmetic, $1.25tn is 46.7 per cent above the March valuation and 10.7 per cent below the $1.4tn first pitched for this round.The public market moved the other way first. The Nasdaq Composite fell 747.73 points, or 2.86 per cent, to 25,437.00 on Friday, its largest one-day percentage drop since 5 June, after weak results from Intel and Amazon, Reuters reported. Intel's shares fell about 28.6 per cent. The S&P 500 lost 1.82 per cent to 7,580.07 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average 1.09 per cent to 51,770.31. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq ended October lower, while the Dow finished the month up.
Nasdaq Composite closeLevelChange to Friday's close, by our arithmetic
30 September (end of September)26,861.06-5.3 per cent

Sources: Federal Reserve Bank of St Louis (FRED) daily closes to 29 October; Friday's close from Reuters. Percentages are Komposite's arithmetic.Set side by side, the two prices have not moved by the same amount. Since Reuters first reported the $30bn round, the Nasdaq Composite has fallen 3.8 per cent by our arithmetic, while the valuation OpenAI is seeking has come down 10.7 per cent. The private price is not set by trading, so the comparison is loose, but it is the clearest measure available of how far demand for the largest private AI company has cooled against the listed market.
OpenAI is pursuing a stock market listing in 2027, and it wants this round closed before Anthropic lists, Reuters said, because the two companies draw on many of the same investors. Anthropic made its registration statement public on Monday, showing first-half revenue of $16.3bn and a net loss of $80.7bn. Its borrowing outlook has also shifted. Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63bn deal financing Anthropic's chips, has told investors it expects Anthropic to receive a "high" junk rating, double-B, after its listing, having earlier predicted an investment-grade rating before 2027, the FT reported, according to TechCrunch. TechCrunch noted that "Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction"; Anthropic and Blackstone declined to comment.
Why it matters: the two largest private AI labs are raising equity and debt in the same weeks that public investors are marking down the companies that supply and host them. Amazon spent $77.3bn on property and equipment in its third quarter, 182 per cent of its operating cash flow, and Alphabet raised $41.1bn of debt and stock to cover its own build-out. A smaller round at a lower price does not change what OpenAI must spend; it changes how much of the company it gives up to pay for it, as Komposite noted when the round was first reported at $30bn.

# Chainalysis reports its own intruder

URL: https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/chainalysis-reports-its-own-intruder/
Section: Cybersecurity
By: Sam Porter
Published: 2026-10-31T13:40:00Z
Updated: 2026-10-31T13:40:00Z

Chainalysis said an attacker using agentic techniques reached internal tools and customer names, emails and roles, but not investigation data or credentials.

Chainalysis, the blockchain analytics company, said an outside attacker using "offensive agentic techniques" gained access to its systems and internal tools and reached customers' names and email addresses, in a security notice dated Friday. It said it had found no evidence that investigation data or login credentials were accessed.
The data reached, according to the notice, was user IDs, names, email addresses and organisation role labels, which The Block described as belonging to provisioned users, the staff that client organisations set up on the platform. Chainalysis said it had found no evidence of access to investigation content such as graphs, notes and cases, to query results, or to clear-text passwords, multi-factor authentication secrets or session tokens, on the evidence "available to date". It is still working out which records belonged to which customer and said it would send each organisation its own update. The company said the intrusion was "not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance".
Chainalysis published the notice, together with the email it sent customers, at about 5:14pm Eastern time on Friday, BleepingComputer reported, and a spokesperson confirmed the incident to the publication. The breach was first flagged by International Cyber Digest, The Block reported. The company has brought in outside cybersecurity specialists, is using large language models in a wider review of its platform and is patching vulnerabilities. It advised customers to turn on two-factor authentication and to watch for unexpected password-reset requests or sign-in prompts, and warned of scammers impersonating the company, particularly those offering to recover funds or to recruit.
CategoryWhat Chainalysis has said
ReachedUser IDs, full names, email addresses and organisation role labels of provisioned users
No evidence of access, on evidence available to dateInvestigation content (graphs, notes, cases), transaction and query results, clear-text passwords, MFA secrets, session tokens
Not disclosedWhen the intrusion was detected beyond "this month", how many customers are affected, which vulnerabilities and internal tools were involved, how long the attacker had access, how AI agents were used, who the attacker is
PromisedAn organisation-by-organisation account of which records were accessed
Compiled by Komposite from Chainalysis's notice and the lists of undisclosed details published by The Block and BleepingComputer."Agentic" describes AI systems that plan and carry out multi-step tasks, such as scanning, logging in and moving between tools, with limited human direction. Chainalysis has not said how such techniques were used against it. BleepingComputer noted that it is unclear whether the attacker used an existing framework such as ARTEX or custom agents. Chainalysis declined to answer specific follow-up questions from The Block, which listed what the company had not disclosed: when it detected the intrusion, how many customers were affected, which vulnerabilities were exploited, the attacker's identity, and the evidence behind its statement that the incident was unrelated to Binance.
This is the third disclosure of an agent-assisted intrusion in ten days, by our count of Komposite's own reporting. On 21 October Microsoft said a China state-aligned group had used an open-source agent framework to try more than 2,250 customer tenants after breaking into ConnectWise's cloud backup service. On Thursday CrowdStrike said a group it calls Vapor Panda used the ARTEX framework against more than 200 organisations, nine of them confirmed compromised. In the first two, the disclosure came from the investigator; this time it comes from the company that was breached, and one whose business is investigation.
The timing is awkward. Chainalysis is one of the firms tracing the funds stolen from Binance, a theft it puts at $6.4bn. On Saturday it said the thieves had moved stablecoins through JustLend, a lending protocol on the Tron blockchain, and swapped them for ether, writing that "now the exploiter is free of worry of a freeze", The Block reported. Issuers such as Circle and Tether have frozen about $2.8bn of stablecoins, Chainalysis said.
Why it matters: the records taken are not secrets, but together they form a directory of who at Chainalysis's client organisations uses a crypto-tracing service, and in what role. That is the material targeted phishing is built from, which is why the company's own advice centres on password-reset prompts and impersonators. Binance's loss began with one engineer's laptop, as Komposite reported on Friday.

# Offshore perps, an onshore operator

URL: https://kompositenews.com/crypto/offshore-perps-an-onshore-operator/
Section: Crypto
By: Marcus Oyelaran
Published: 2026-10-31T13:20:00Z
Updated: 2026-10-31T13:20:00Z

ICE agreed to operate US-regulated versions of Trade[XYZ]'s Hyperliquid perpetual futures and take a minority stake, pending approval and with no date.

Intercontinental Exchange, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, has signed a definitive agreement to operate US-regulated versions of Trade[XYZ]'s perpetual futures markets, which run on the Hyperliquid blockchain, and is taking a minority stake in the company, ICE said on Thursday. The plan needs regulatory approval.
A perpetual future is a futures contract with no expiry date. Instead of settling on a fixed day, it is held close to the price of the underlying asset by periodic payments between buyers and sellers. Trade[XYZ] uses Hyperliquid to offer eligible non-US users round-the-clock contracts on shares, equity indices, commodities and currencies. ICE will be the exclusive operator of the regulated versions and plans a new market and clearing structure dedicated to retail traders, with identity and anti-money-laundering checks, and will seek approval to support leveraged trading, the release says. CoinDesk reported that the venue, called ICE[XYZ], would also list crypto contracts.
PartyRole under the agreement
HyperliquidUnderlying trading infrastructure, through its HIP-3 framework for builder-deployed markets
Trade[XYZ]Designs the contracts; keeps running its existing markets for eligible non-US users
ICEExclusive operator of the US-regulated markets; builds a dedicated retail market and clearing structure; minority investor in Trade[XYZ]
Futures commission merchantsBecome members and give verified customers access
ICE-OKX joint ventureOne distribution channel, pending its own approvals as a US broker-dealer and futures commission merchant
RegulatorsMust approve the market, the clearing structure and leveraged trading; no timetable given
Compiled by Komposite from ICE's announcement and The Block's description of the structure.ICE is careful to keep the new business apart from its old one. The retail market would run separately from its institutional futures and clearing operations, and the company says its commercial hedgers and institutional customers would have no exposure to retail trading or counterparty risk. Customers would reach the markets through futures commission merchants that become members, and through partners including ICE's joint venture with OKX, which itself is awaiting approval as a US broker-dealer and futures commission merchant. ICE says its existing business is more than 99 per cent institutional.
"We see these perp markets as additive to our futures markets, not a replacement for them," Jeffrey Sprecher, ICE's chair and chief executive, said in the release. He also pointed to a clear rise in retail participation, often around the clock, The Block reported. Trade[XYZ] described the planned market as "a new venue for price discovery, open whenever the world moves." Neither company disclosed the size of the stake. ICE said it was not expected to have a material effect on its 2026 adjusted results, capital return or plans to reduce debt.
Trade[XYZ] says its markets on Hyperliquid have handled more than $650bn of trading in just over a year, CoinDesk reported. By our arithmetic, taking "just over a year" as 13 months, that is no more than about $50bn a month on average. Open interest across HIP-3 markets, the Hyperliquid framework that lets outside builders such as Trade[XYZ] deploy contracts, reached $2.38bn in April, according to The Block. Hyperliquid's HYPE token rose about 15 per cent on Thursday to around $91, The Block said; CoinDesk later put the day's gain at nearly 20 per cent.
The deal also brought a new name to the venture. Stanley Druckenmiller, the investor, used his first post on X to say he had invested in Trade[XYZ], without giving an amount, CoinDesk reported. He wrote that the partnership would bring "24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States", according to The Block. Jeff Yan, a Hyperliquid co-founder, wrote that he "could never have predicted the progress that we've made as a community in a single year to make this come true."
The regulatory path is open but contested. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued a staff advisory and no-action relief for US perpetual futures in May, The Block reported. CME Group sued the CFTC in June, arguing that perpetual contracts were wrongly classified as futures rather than swaps, and the regulator has asked the court to dismiss the case, CoinDesk reported. Neither ICE nor Trade[XYZ] has said when the markets could open or who will be eligible.
Why it matters: the two largest US futures exchange groups have now taken opposite positions on the same product. CME is in court arguing that the CFTC should not have approved a perpetual, as Komposite reported when the regulator answered CME's challenge. ICE, which has also invested in OKX and in Polymarket, is building a retail venue on a crypto chain's rails. The CFTC's approach to event contracts has already brought sports leagues to prediction markets; perpetuals on shares and commodities would extend that reach to round-the-clock leveraged trading.

# A million fewer search visits a week

URL: https://kompositenews.com/ai/a-million-fewer-search-visits-a-week/
Section: AI
By: Dana Whitfield
Published: 2026-10-30T16:40:00Z
Updated: 2026-10-30T16:40:00Z

Reddit said search referrals fell sharply as search turns to AI, warned daily users could drop in Q4 and guided below forecasts. Shares fell about 25%.

Reddit said on Thursday that visits from search engines fell "meaningfully" in the third quarter as search becomes an AI-powered destination, and that its daily users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage this quarter, according to its letter to shareholders. Its shares fell about a quarter on Friday.
The quarter itself was strong. Revenue rose 53 per cent to $895m, advertising revenue 54 per cent to $847m and net income 74 per cent to $283m, or $1.40 a diluted share, the results release shows. Adjusted EBITDA was $402m, a margin of 44.9 per cent. Daily active uniques, the company's main user measure, rose 12 per cent to 130.3m, but fell 2 per cent in the United States to 50.7m. For the fourth quarter Reddit guided revenue of $1,000m to $1,030m and adjusted EBITDA of $480m to $510m.
The letter is unusually direct. "Our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter," it says. "During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week." The biggest effect was on logged-out and web visitors, Reddit said, though some flowed through to logged-in and app users, since "search referral is a common source of reengagement for users". It added: "If this rate of decline continues, current trends would suggest that total DAUqs could fall in Q4, by a low-double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUqs."
Reddit daily active uniques, Q3 2026United StatesInternationalGlobal
Logged-in23.4m (up 1 per cent)30.1m (up 11 per cent)53.5m (up 7 per cent)
Logged-out27.3m (down 4 per cent)49.5m (up 33 per cent)76.8m (up 17 per cent)
Total50.7m (down 2 per cent)79.6m (up 24 per cent)130.3m (up 12 per cent)
Average revenue per user$13.82 (up 53 per cent)$2.43 (up 32 per cent)$6.87 (up 36 per cent)
Source: Reddit's third-quarter release and shareholder letter, 29 October 2026; changes are year on year. By our arithmetic, logged-out users are 59 per cent of the global total and 54 per cent of the US total.The letter does not name Google. It describes the change in general terms: "Web search is evolving from a gateway to the web to becoming an AI-powered destination itself." Reddit's answer is to depend less on visitors who never sign in. "In Q4 we'll begin fully testing this in select markets outside the U.S.," the letter says of a logged-in-only Reddit, adding that "it is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting". Steve Huffman, the founder and chief executive, said in the release that "the Reddit experience captures the human experience in a way that no other platform can replicate".
Investors looked past the quarter. Analysts had expected fourth-quarter revenue of $1.05bn, Investing.com reported, and the shares fell about 22 per cent shortly after Friday's open. KeyBanc cut the stock to Sector Weight, writing that "our thesis is not playing out; search traffic is a larger headwind than envisioned", and Citizens cut it to Market Perform. John Colantuoni of Jefferies wrote that "delivery of strong Revenue/EBITDA growth (53%/70%) was overshadowed by worsening U.S. DAU declines". The fall reached 25 per cent, Yahoo Finance reported, which noted the shares had closed on Thursday at about 15 times forward earnings against a one-year average of 26.
By our arithmetic, the guidance midpoint of $1,015m is 3.3 per cent below that consensus but still 13.4 per cent above the third quarter, at an implied adjusted EBITDA margin of about 49 per cent. Logged-out users, the group most exposed to search, are 59 per cent of daily users worldwide and 54 per cent in the United States. Reading "low-double-digit" as 10 to 13 per cent, the warning implies 113m to 117m daily users if the October trend holds. Revenue per US user, $13.82, is 5.7 times the international figure, which is why a 2 per cent fall at home weighs more than a 24 per cent rise abroad.
Why it matters: Reddit has now put a weekly number on the traffic it is losing as search changes, in a document filed with its regulator. Alphabet's search revenue rose 12 per cent to $63.4bn in the quarter, Yahoo Finance noted, even as Alphabet's own shares fell on spending that ran ahead of its cash. The visits that once followed a search result are increasingly kept inside the answer, which is the market a new class of start-ups is trying to sell into, as Komposite reported when Profound raised $180m to get brands named in AI answers.

# Eighty-five per cent margins, and an eight-for-one split

URL: https://kompositenews.com/markets/eighty-five-per-cent-margins-and-an-eight-for-one-split/
Section: Markets
By: Priya Raghavan
Published: 2026-10-30T16:20:00Z
Updated: 2026-10-30T16:20:00Z

Sandisk's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 378% to $11.0bn at an 85% gross margin. It guided to $12.4bn and set an 8-for-1 stock split from 20 November.

Sandisk, the flash memory maker, reported revenue of $11.0bn for its fiscal first quarter on Thursday, up 378 per cent from a year earlier, at a gross margin of 85 per cent, according to its results release. It also announced an eight-for-one stock split.
Revenue for the quarter to 2 October was $11,031m, against $8,965m in the previous quarter and $2,308m a year earlier. GAAP operating income was $8,780m, up from $176m, and GAAP net income was $8,101m, or $52.60 a diluted share; on Sandisk's non-GAAP measure, earnings were $49.51 a share. The GAAP gross margin was 85.0 per cent, against 29.8 per cent a year before. Operating cash flow was $6,363m and free cash flow $6,309m. For the second quarter Sandisk guided revenue of $12.2bn to $12.6bn, a non-GAAP gross margin of 84.5 to 85.5 per cent and non-GAAP earnings of $55 to $57 a share before the split.
"We have started fiscal year 2027 with another quarter of strong performance, with robust and growing demand for our products driving outpaced growth in our data center business," David Goeckeler, the chairman and chief executive, said in the release. Datacenter revenue rose 61 per cent from the previous quarter to $4,802m. Edge, which covers flash sold into phones, PCs and other devices, rose 7 per cent to $5,832m. Consumer products fell 29 per cent to $397m.

Shares and multiples are Komposite's arithmetic.On the call, Goeckeler said customers "have underestimated the amount of NAND they need", and that "we have multiple customers coming back for a second round", 24/7 Wall St. reported. Sandisk calls its long-term supply contracts, which include customer prepayments, its "new business model". It had signed eight by its August investor day, covering about half of fiscal 2027 output and about two-thirds of fiscal 2028, and closed two more in the quarter, the report said. Management told analysts: "Our NBM pipeline exceeds our supply throughout the end of the decade." Luis Visoso, the chief financial officer, said pricing was expected to rise only "modestly".
Analysts had expected revenue of $10.7bn, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence figures cited by Yahoo Finance, and the midpoints of both revenue and earnings guidance were above Street forecasts of $12.23bn and $53.30 a share. The shares had closed Thursday's regular session at $1,330.05, down 5.3 per cent, before the release. Yahoo Finance noted that the stock was up more than 460 per cent this year but had "largely treaded water since July".
The split is mechanical but not trivial. Holders of record at the close on Monday 9 November receive seven additional shares for each share held after the close on Thursday 19 November, and the stock trades on a split-adjusted basis from Friday 20 November. By our arithmetic, Thursday's close becomes about $166 a share, and the guidance midpoint of $56 becomes about $7.00 a share on the new count. The split comes after a quarter in which Sandisk spent $5.0bn repurchasing about 3.2m shares, 79 per cent of its free cash flow by our arithmetic, and 6.0m shares, about 4 per cent of its stock, over two quarters.
By our arithmetic, the datacenter business has gone from 11.7 per cent of revenue to 43.5 per cent in a year, and is 18 times its size a year ago. GAAP operating income was 79.6 per cent of revenue. Guidance implies another 12 per cent of sequential growth at the midpoint, with no margin give-back. The guidance is the company's own, and its support is contractual rather than cyclical: the long-term agreements already cover about half of this fiscal year's output and about two-thirds of next year's, on 24/7 Wall St.'s account of the call.
Why it matters: the memory shortage has two sides. For the makers of memory it is the best market in their history, as Samsung's record quarterly profit forecast showed this month. For those who buy it, it is a cost: Intel on Thursday blamed "the unprecedented memory crunch" for a shrinking PC market, and its shares fell by about a fifth after hours, as Komposite reported on Friday. Sandisk's own consumer revenue fell 39 per cent from a year earlier.
